text: If a thief is caught breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.

versions.text: If a thief is caught breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew 'lo' refers to the person who struck the thief, not to the deed. 'For it' is vague; 'for him' matches the Hebrew and parallels the phrasing of the next verse ('there is bloodguilt').

text: But if the sun has risen on him, there is bloodguilt. The thief must make full restitution; if he has nothing, he shall be sold to pay for his theft.
If what he stole is found alive in his possession, whether ox or donkey or sheep, he shall pay back double.

If a man puts his livestock into a field or a vineyard, and lets them loose so that they feed in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.

versions.text: If a man lets his livestock graze a field or a vineyard, and turns them loose so that they graze in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
versions.explanation: The word 'graze' appears twice in quick succession, which stumbles when read aloud. Varying the verbs keeps the sense while improving the rhythm.

text: If a fire breaks out and spreads through thornbushes, so that stacked grain or standing grain or a whole field is consumed, the one who started the fire shall make full restitution.
If a man gives his neighbor silver or goods for safekeeping, and they are stolen from the man's house, then if the thief is found, he shall pay back double.

versions.text: If a man gives his neighbor silver or goods for safekeeping, and they are stolen from the man's house, the thief, if he is found, shall pay back double.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew clause order is conditional ('if the thief is found, he shall pay double'). The interrupted subject in the current rendering is awkward for oral reading.

text: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house shall be brought before God, to determine whether he has laid his hand on his neighbor's property. [Footnote: Or 'before the judges'; the Hebrew word can refer to God or to those who judge in his name.]

versions.text: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house shall be brought before God, to determine whether he has laid his hand on his neighbor's property.
versions.explanation: 'ha-Elohim' here is widely understood either as God himself or as the judges acting in his name. A short footnote clarifies the legal setting without changing the rendering.

text: In every case of dishonesty, whether it concerns an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims as his own, the case of both parties shall come before God. The one whom God declares guilty shall pay back double to his neighbor.
If a man gives his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal for safekeeping, and it dies or is injured or is driven off with no one to see it,
an oath before the LORD shall settle the matter between them, that he has not laid his hand on his neighbor's property. The owner shall accept this, and no restitution shall be made.
But if it was in fact stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
If it was torn by wild animals, let him bring the remains as evidence; he need not pay for what was torn.
If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies while its owner is not present, he shall make full restitution.
If the owner was present, no restitution shall be made. If the animal was hired, the loss is covered by the hiring fee.
If a man seduces a virgin who is not engaged and lies with her, he must pay the bride-price and take her as his wife.
If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he must still weigh out silver equal to the bride-price for virgins.
You shall not let a sorceress live.
Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.
Whoever sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone shall be devoted to destruction.
You shall not wrong a foreigner or oppress him, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.
My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword; your wives will become widows and your children fatherless.
If you lend money to my people, to the poor among you, do not act as a creditor toward them; you shall not charge them interest.
If you take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, return it to him before the sun goes down,
for it is his only covering, the garment for his body. What else does he have to sleep in? And when he cries out to me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
You shall not revile God, nor curse a leader of your people.
Do not hold back the offering from your harvest or your winepress. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to me.
Do the same with your cattle and your sheep: seven days the newborn shall stay with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
You shall be holy people to me. You shall not eat the meat of an animal torn by beasts in the field; throw it to the dogs.
